{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Patch testing requires 3 additional visits during screening, increasing burden",
      "quote": "Patients will be called to the site for 3 visits for the patch testing",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The schedule already includes a screening visit (V1) and a separate V1a for patch testing, but the text specifies 3 visits for patch testing alone, which is not reflected in the SoA and adds significant patient burden.",
      "fix": "Clarify in the SoA that patch testing requires 3 visits, or consider consolidating to fewer visits if possible."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing washout periods may delay screening and are not specified in SoA",
      "quote": "Patients need to discontinue therapies for AD before the patch testing is conducted. The wash out period will be as follows: 1 week for TCS/TCI /topical JAK inhibitor/crisaborole application... 4 weeks for oral corticosteroids... 4 weeks for other systemic immunomodulators",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The washout periods (up to 4 weeks) are not reflected in the SoA's screening window (D-56 to D-1), which may be insufficient for patients requiring 4-week washouts, leading to rescreening or protocol deviations.",
      "fix": "Ensure the screening window accommodates required washouts or specify that screening may be extended."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing reading at day 3-7 conflicts with scheduled visits",
      "quote": "Appointment 3 (reading of results at day 3 to day 7): A second reading will be taken",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The SoA shows V1a for patch testing but does not specify the timing of the 3 appointments. The day 3-7 reading may fall outside the V1a window, causing scheduling conflicts.",
      "fix": "Align the SoA with the patch testing visit schedule, possibly by adding a dedicated visit or clarifying that V1a includes multiple appointments."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing results may not be available before randomization if V1a is too close to baseline",
      "quote": "Patch testing should normally be conducted after other screening procedures (eg, lab testing) have been completed and eligibility for the study confirmed.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "If patch testing is done after eligibility is confirmed, and the final reading is at day 3-7, randomization at V2 (Day 1) may occur before results are available, risking enrollment of ineligible patients.",
      "fix": "Ensure the SoA allows sufficient time between V1a and V2 for patch test results, or specify that randomization is delayed until results are known."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing on upper back may be impractical for patients with extensive AD",
      "quote": "The patch test should be applied on normal appearing skin free from skin diseases such as AD. The upper back is preferred site for the application of patch tests.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Patients with hand and foot dermatitis may have AD on the upper back, making it difficult to find normal skin for patch testing, potentially leading to site challenges.",
      "fix": "Provide guidance on alternative sites or allow flexibility in patch test location."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing reading criteria may be subjective and require training",
      "quote": "The patch tests will be read using the globally recognized the ICDRG criteria:",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The ICDRG criteria require interpretation (e.g., distinguishing irritant vs. allergic reactions), which may lead to variability across sites; training is essential.",
      "fix": "Include mandatory training and central reading if possible to ensure consistency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing with personal products may increase complexity and burden",
      "quote": "In addition, patch testing with extended baseline series, supplemental series and/or personal products may be carried out as per clinical judgment of investigator.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Additional patch testing with personal products can increase the number of allergens and visits, adding burden and potential for adverse reactions.",
      "fix": "Limit additional testing to cases where clinically necessary and document in the protocol."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing may require additional visits beyond the 3 specified",
      "quote": "In some patients a reading after day 7 may be taken when the clinical history strongly supports sensitization.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The possibility of a reading after day 7 adds an unscheduled visit, increasing patient burden and scheduling complexity.",
      "fix": "Clarify that such readings are optional and should be minimized to reduce burden."
    }
  ]
}
